chapter_title: Concerning the Five Wonders that the Light Mind shall display in the Elect
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by institutional/ethical material (the elect preaching, faith, love, peace for brethren, and legal excommunication in the church). Only one short paragraph (¶7) reads like an impersonal cosmological-soteriological mechanism (Light Mind acting upon the new man) without direct institutional anchoring. The ending (¶9) uses strongly NT-sounding idiom (“vessel”, “pearl without price”), suggesting Christian overlay or late devotional diction.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic attribution (“Once again the apostle speaks”) is a compilation frame marker; “apostle” is explicitly Layer-2/3 Kephalaia apparatus.
A fivefold list of virtues enacted by the elect through preaching; the mapping is not cosmos→cosmos but behavior within the community (“preach and proclaim”).
Continues virtue-listing in community/hearing-believing register; this is catechetical/institutional rhetoric rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
Even through lacunae, the pivot is explicitly communal (“peace of heart for the assembly of his brethren”), an application-to-community register.
Ethical exhortation in immediate social setting (“brothers and sisters who are seated [before] him”); not an internal cosmic correspondence.
Explicit church discipline vocabulary (“legal excommunication”, “found in the church”) is institutional material; this is the clearest pastoral layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The Light Mind puts these five signs in the new man, [whom he has] purified, cleansed, supported and chosen [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, mechanism-like statement about a named cosmological entity (the Light Mind) acting to produce/establish qualities in the ‘new man’, without direct reference to church offices/discipline. Some uncertainty remains because it presupposes the preceding virtue-list, but the sentence itself stays within a soteriological-cosmic agency register.
Beatitude-style exhortation (“Blessed is every one … is diligent”) addresses the hearer’s piety; application voice rather than structural cosmology.

Devotional climax with idioms that strongly echo NT language (“vessel”; “pearl without price” ≈ ‘pearl of great price’). The lead-in (“The [other] one:”) also signals a later dialogue/redactional presentation rather than substrate exposition.
